item.title: Virginia county sues to block President Donald Trump from building his 250-foot-tall triumphal arch
item.description: Arlington County’s all-Democratic board argues in a lawsuit filed in federal court in Virginia that the Trump administration failed to adequately evaluate potential environmental impacts of the project as required by federal law. The administration plans to build the arch on an island in the Potomac River that is officially part of D.C. but is within a few hundred yards of Arlington, a county of about 240,000 people that is home to several federal agencies.

item.title: At 81, he’s the most-cited nutrition expert. Here’s what he eats in a day.
item.description: Walter Willett’s research has changed the way Americans eat, revealing how diet and other lifestyle choices can shape your risk of chronic illnesses.

item.title: Fort Hood shooter’s execution by firing squad will be livestreamed, Defense Department says
item.description: The announcement came after earlier comments Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth made indicating he wanted the execution of Nidal Malik Hasan to be public. Hasan is a former U.S. Army psychiatrist who opened fire on dozens of people at Fort Hood, Texas, in 2009, killing 13 people and injuring 32 others.

item.title: Why are fewer teens identifying as gay or bisexual? Researchers aren’t sure.
item.description: The decline is particularly striking among ninth-grade girls, according to Jean Twenge, a professor of psychology at San Diego State University, who analyzed Centers for Disease Control and Prevention data.

item.description: Vice President JD Vance announced the suspension, saying it would affect H-1B visas and aims to protect U.S. workers.

item.title: Search warrants against the former prince Andrew were unlawful, court finds, but misconduct investigation may continue
item.description: British police acknowledged applying for the warrants under the wrong statutory provision, the judge said. King Charles III’s brother was taken into custody in February over suspicions of misconduct in public office connected to his relationship with the convicted child sex offender Jeffrey Epstein.

item.title: Army report cites systemic flaws that led to Black Hawk helicopter’s fatal 2025 collision with airliner in D.C.
item.description: The documents, reviewed by The Post ahead of public dissemination, detail numerous shortfalls in Army procedures and policy that investigators said contributed to the tragedy, which killed 67 people.

item.description: Police officers helping ICE arrest unauthorized immigrants were given a shortened training course, and instruction providing officers with real world scenarios they might encounter was eliminated altogether, according to emails reviewed by The Washington Post.

item.description: In addition to co-starring with Marlon Brando in “On the Waterfront,” she played a chic seductress opposite Cary Grant in “North by Northwest.”

item.title: Christa Pike is conscious and speaking after last week’s failed execution in Tennessee, attorneys say
item.description: Her attorneys said in a joint statement Tuesday that Pike is still handcuffed and shackled to a bed at a Nashville-area hospital “despite the severe damage she endured to her arms” during the attempted execution by lethal injection.

item.title: D.C. Council approves $305 million for Metro, bus upgrades near future Commanders stadium on former RFK site
item.description: Nearly all of that money — $300 million — will go to the WMATA for improvements at the nearby Stadium-Armory rail station to help accommodate the expected increase in visitors to the area. The work is set to be completed in time for the scheduled opening of the new stadium in 2030.

item.title: Jim Bakker dies at 86. The former televangelist was tarnished by a sex sandal and a conviction for fraud and conspiracy.
item.description: Bakker was a preacher and fundraiser on television for more than 20 years, developing a following that numbered in the millions. He and his wife were at the peak of their popularity in March 1987, when the Charlotte Observer revealed that Mr. Bakker had a brief sexual encounter in 1980 with Jessica Hahn, a 21-year-old church secretary from New York.

item.title: Trump reverses course, says he won’t use taxpayer money for campaign-style ads
item.description: The president has faced backlash from Democrats and even some Republicans about the commercials. The president argued that the television spots, which included one that closely resembled an ad for his 2024 presidential campaign, and another of him and Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth advocating for the Iran war, were “a rather standard thing to do.” But he said he had “decided to do the Patriotic Ads, among others, and pay for them myself, and with money I raised for MAGA, Inc.”

item.title: Activists sat atop a ‘grandmother’ tree for months. Border agents just knocked it down.
item.description: The activists were trying to block President Donald Trump’s $46.5 billion border wall expansion. They say more than 50 Customs and Border Protection agents raided their camp Monday and an excavator knocked down the tree, estimated to be 150 to 250 years old.

item.description: After more than two hours of argument, it was unclear whether the justices would green-light Boulder, Colorado’s novel lawsuit against ExxonMobil and Suncor Energy.
